title: Sowing and planting A sound start

approval.scope: Page 163 proof and all three revision 04 photographs

brief: Direct sowing in a row in open soil; module seedlings on the greenhouse bench; planting a hardened-off lettuce plug into open garden soil.
setting: The near, porch end is used for direct sowing. The lettuce plugs go at the opposite, greenhouse end close to the transverse timber bed. The module-tray photograph is on the greenhouse bench.

outdoor_generation.prompt:
Create TWO new outdoor photographs as ONE photographic diptych, 2:1 landscape canvas split exactly in half into two equally sized square photographs, without gutters, captions, letters or graphic overlays. For John Lennon's book The Vegetable Guru. The most important correction is PHYSICAL GEOGRAPHY: the gardener is working at OPPOSITE SHORT ENDS of one and the same long garden bed, separated by several metres. In the finished right photograph the previously sown area ALSO has to be visible, unoccupied, in the foreground, so the reader can SEE that no lettuce is being planted in the seed drill. Do not use two repeated close positions alongside the same edging. Show John full figure in both views, knees, boots, head and his action inside each square. Shot by a friend on two real work days in Cornwall: ordinary candid, tactile, naturally untidy garden.

REFERENCE 1 is the REAL view with A and B plotted on the actual bed footprint. The dots are exact physical locations of the HANDS doing the jobs; borrow the geography, NEVER include graphics. A = near short end closest to the photographer/porch; B = remote short end adjoining the transverse timber bed and back fence. Reference 2 independently fixes the length, far end and location of the greenhouse. Convert cardboard and compost heaps to continuous cultivated soil. Keep only low garden bed edging as pictured. The porch itself is behind the camera. Reference 3 is previous full-figure pictures: use only John’s likeness, full figure scale, photographic realism and clothes. Both its events occurred in the same part of the bed; that spatial layout MUST change completely. Reference 4 actual lowered-profile guide is authoritative: John has a high receding hairline and a quite receding chin well BEHIND the lower lip, short grey beard receding into the collar, no prominent square jaw. Reference 5 pairs John’s actual working clothes. Preserve same man and garden in both.

COMPOSITION 1: LOOK LENGTHWISE from the porch side along the narrow bed, with its near short edge crossing the lower foreground; three-quarter view of John in oatmeal jumper, bareheaded, worn jeans, worn boots. Kneeling on the grass at the NEAR-LEFT CORNER beside the short front end, next to the first few light grey edging blocks and towards the terracotta pots side. One foot planted and one knee down, he holds an opened paper carrot-seed packet in his left hand and sows thinly with right forefinger and thumb near the soil. Sowing into a SHORT SHALLOW ROW running ACROSS the width of the bed, parallel and just inside this near short edge. Tiny seeds are credible and barely visible from camera distance. Place one modest, slightly leaning, pale wooden plant marker at the lawn-side head of this row. The bed continues empty for several metres BEHIND his working hand to the unoccupied remote end. Do not show lettuces in this first photo. Keep a sliver of blue shed and the real greenhouse beyond, brick base, berry planter, rough patches in actual lawn. This is a person-sized, settled back-garden bed.

COMPOSITION 2: A new photo a few weeks later. The photographer is still at the PORCH SIDE looking down the same bed. Frame with the bed running diagonally from BOTTOM LEFT up to the UPPER RIGHT. Now draw John at B, the OTHER END, with his boots on the narrow CROSS-PATH just BEYOND THE FAR SHORT EDGE. Place him backed by the actual rear transverse timber bed with its leafy kale, alongside the greenhouse's far corner, nearer the fence. Turn him three-quarters toward the camera, leaning over the far short edge to plant back towards the lens. Kneeling posture relaxed, navy pullover, worn work jeans and boots all in view. This must produce a strikingly different composition from the first image: the LONG BED now extends IN FRONT OF John toward the camera, and John is at its TOP end. Compose with his body to the UPPER RIGHT and the seed-sown near area visibly unoccupied in the LOWER LEFT. One or two short, fine rows of tiny wispy emerging CARROT SEEDLINGS with the SAME leaning wooden marker occupy the near foreground. The midsection is continuous open earth. Several metres away, he holds ONE root plug of Little Gem lettuce by its dark sides, lowering it into a planting hole at the distant end. Two lettuce plugs already planted BESIDE HIM in that far third, black half-used module tray on the path beside his boot. A slightly tighter focal length if necessary so his full kneeling figure there still occupies 40–50% of the image height; task and lettuce readable at small print size. The emerging carrot rows are visually delicate and clearly separate from the lettuce patch. Absolutely no lettuces or gardener at the NEAR marker in this image.

Ensure different silhouettes, near-left vs far-right compositions, different neighbouring landmarks and a credible long stretch of continuous garden soil between patches. Preserve greenhouse and fence positions from real location images without mirroring. Outdoor natural light a little brighter in picture 2, authentic local soil with crumbly tilth and compost flecks. No diagrams, no labels, no artificially staged tools or horticultural showroom symmetry. It should feel like the reader has watched John move from one end of his own garden bed to the other on two different days.
